title: B cell receptor-induced protein dynamics and the emerging role of SUMOylation revealed by proximity proteomics
projectDescription: In this study, we used proximity labelling technique (APEX2) to study early protein dynamics in the vicinity of B cell receptor upon antigen engagement.
sampleProcessingProtocol: A20 B cells stably expressing raft-APEX2 were activated with potent surrogate antigen, F(ab’)2 fragments of anti-IgM antibodies for 0, 5, 10 or 15 min. Cells were supplemented with biotin-phenol and biotinylation was then triggered by addition of 1 mM H2O2. Biotinylation was then quenched with addition of Trolox after 1 min. Cells were lysed and subjected to streptavidin affinity purification to pull down the biotinylated proteins for LC-MS/MS analysis. To control for both baseline activity of the APEX2 and endogenous biotinylation, samples without H2O2 or without biotin-phenol were prepared, respectively. All conditions were performed in triplicates. Trypsin-digested samples were analyzed with a high resolution LC-MS/MS (Lumos, Thermo Scientific).
dataProcessingProtocol: Trypsin-digested samples subjected to LC-MS/MS using Orbitrap Fusion Lumos (Thermo Scientific).Raw files were analyzed using MaxQuant version 1.6.0.1.
